question: Ten Fundamental Duties have been added in Part-IV of the Constitution under ________ in the year 1976 through the 42ⁿd Constitutional Amendment.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 51A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 added a new part IV-A to the Indian Constitution, which enshrines the Fundamental Duties of citizens.
 
• Article 51A, specifically, lists ten Fundamental Duties for every citizen of India.
 
• These duties include respecting the Constitution, the national flag, and the national anthem; cherishing the noble ideals of the freedom struggle; and upholding and protecting the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• Other duties involve promoting harmony, safeguarding public property, protecting the environment, and striving towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Amendments:**

 
 
• Constitutional amendments are changes made to the Constitution to address issues or update its provisions. The Constitution of India provides a detailed process for amendments under Article 368.
 
• The 42nd Amendment, enacted in 1976, is one of the most significant amendments as it brought about extensive changes, including the addition of the Fundamental Duties.
 
 
 
• **Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• Part IV-A was added to the Constitution through the 42nd Amendment and it deals with Fundamental Duties. This part aims to remind citizens that while they enjoy their rights, they also have certain duties to perform.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR. They are non-justiciable, which means they are not enforceable by the courts for their violation.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Fundamental Duties:**
 
 
• The inclusion of Fundamental Duties was intended to serve as a constant reminder to citizens that they should be conscious of their duties towards their country, society, and fellow citizens.
 
• These duties help in promoting a sense of discipline and commitment among citizens, which is essential for the unity and integrity of the nation.
